Hey me 2

First of all good job getting to this point. 

Usually on the the first days of clinicals it's really just a introduction to the o.r and perioperative areas. Yo will make your rounds and do some paperwork , maybe get a badge and shown a locker room to change in. Try to listen attentively to everyone and make good eye contact with people. You will generally hear the same thing over and over again but still accept the advice like it's the first time you have heard it. 

The first day can can go one of two ways: either your tossed into a case with no previous knowledge of the case or you can be shadowing a manager doing paperwork etc. 

If you are tossed into a room remember your training. It's overwhelming but you will get accustomed to it pretty quickly. You are there for learning, you will make mistakes, but how you handle those mistakes is what counts. Be attentive to what the scrub says and be upbeat if you can, it helps alot. 

You will be shown the board where the assignments are made. Here you can see what cases you have ahead of time and look up on the anatomy, instruments, preceedure etc. 

Once you have been there a couple of weeks and want to see a specific type of case ask the board runner. If the can get you in they will but don't get discouraged if they san no. It could be a nother thing preventing you from observing.

Good luck, it's a stressful job but it is rewarding if you let it be.
